Runtime notes:
- Play through the `act` tool. One call sends one command in the game's grammar and
  returns what the game says back, the same as the `> command` and observation pairs
  in the examples. Send one command per turn and read its observation before you send
  the next.
- The sandbox is offline and has no pip. You cannot install or download anything.
- The game ends the episode when the task is done or the budget runs out. You can also
  end it yourself by sending `done` through `act`, when you have finished or cannot
  finish. After that, `act` only answers `Episode over`.

<EXEMPLAR>

Runtime notes:
- Each `> exec` in the example is one call of the `exec` tool. Send the code as that
  call, never as reply text, and read its `output:` before the next call. Variables
  persist between calls. `exec` is the only way to reach the apps. Running python3
  from bash does not work.
- The sandbox is offline and has no pip. You cannot install or download anything.
- The episode ends when you call `apis.supervisor.complete_task(...)`, or when the exec
  budget runs out. Call it with `status="fail"` if you cannot finish. After that, `exec`
  only answers `Episode over`.
